title: Manager Shadow Week: 14-day Access Roadmap & Mentor Sprint
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working doc for the manager shadow week: a repeatable 14-day mentor sprint that (1) gets new managers operationally ready, (2) gives mentors a clear shadowing/feedback cadence, and (3) reduces access friction so managers can take on team responsibilities by day 15.

Scope / Intended audience:
- New people managers across engineering, product, and platform teams (first-time and promoted-from-IC).
- Mentor: an experienced manager (peer-level) who will run the 14-day sprint.
- People Ops partner who provisions access and tracks completion.

Quick decisions / triggers:
- Trigger: candidate accepted for manager role OR internal promotion confirmed.
- People Ops assigns a mentor within 48h.
- Manager shadow week starts on first working Monday after access is provisioned. If access delays >3 business days, run a trimmed 10-day sprint.

Pre-boarding checklist (to be completed before Day 1):
- Workspace access: Google Workspace, Slack, Redwood SSO, Okta group membership (manager-level).
- Code and infra access: GitHub team membership, read access to production runbooks, deploy dashboards (staging).
- Console & tools: Redwood Console login + view-only to team routes, cost dashboards, SLO boards.
- HR & payroll: People Ops orientation scheduled, benefits enrollment link.
- Admins: calendar invites sent for recurring 1:1s for first 30 days, mentor weekly sync, skip-level intro.
- Notes to self: include a short bio + expectations in the Slack #team-welcome post (mentor does this).

Day 0 (pre-first-day) - Mentor tasks:
- Confirm all accesses; share a private Evernote/Google Doc called "Manager-Shadow-Evidence" and add the new manager.
- Drop 30-min "what to expect" on calendar with link to this doc and onboarding checklist.

Day 1-3 (orientation + observation):
- Day 1 morning: 1:1 with mentor (30m): role expectations, org map, team charters.
- Day 1 afternoon: shadow team standup + triage session (mentor narrates decisions).
- Day 2: observe 1:1s with direct report (mentor runs, new manager takes notes).
- Day 3: observe a cross-functional planning meeting (mentor highlights stakeholder map).
- Deliverable by EOD Day 3: new manager writes 3 quick wins + 3 risks in evidence doc.

Day 4-7 (hands-on pairing):
- Pair on a small operational task (oncall triage simulation, runbook update, hiring shortlisting).
- Mentor hands control of non-production tasks: approve a minor docs change, run a retrospective blameless postmortem writeup draft.
- Shadow a postmortem or incident review (focus: communication, escalation policy).
- Deliverable by Day 7: draft one runbook or team communication template and get mentor feedback.

Day 8-11 (decision practice & delegation):
- Practice making a low-risk decision end-to-end (e.g., reprioritize a sprint slice, approve prioritization of a bug vs feature). Mentor reviews rationale using the evaluation rubric below.
- Roleplay a difficult upward conversation (mentor plays exec/stakeholder).
- Deliverable by Day 11: evidence doc should have 2 decision writeups and mentor notes.

Day 12-14 (handoff + autonomy check):
- New manager runs an actual team check-in (mentor observes, minimal interjection).
- Mentor runs a calibration session: go over evidence doc, flag any open gaps.
- Final 30-min sign-off meeting: mentor, people ops, new manager. Agree on a 30/60/90 plan and any outstanding access items.

Evaluation Rubric (used by mentor & People Ops):
- Operational readiness (Green/Amber/Red):
  - Green: completed two hands-on tasks independently, demonstrates accurate triage and runbook edits, all required accesses are confirmed.
  - Amber: has completed tasks with coaching and shows consistent improvement, 1 access item remains pending.
  - Red: unable to complete basic ops tasks without repeated intervention, multiple access blockers.
- People management baseline:
  - Green: demonstrates concrete feedback framework, has scheduled 1:1s, demonstrated active listening in roleplays.
  - Amber: shows basic scaffolding but needs refinement on feedback specificity.
  - Red: unclear next steps for direct reports, misses escalation patterns.
- Communication & stakeholder awareness:
  - Green: clear summaries, escalations as needed, stakeholder mapping.
  - Amber: needs help prioritizing stakeholders; occasional unclear updates.
  - Red: reactive, misses key follow-ups.

Scoring: annotate evidence doc with G/A/R for each criteria and include one short paragraph of mentor commentary. People Ops records final status in HRIS with tags: manager-shadow:complete | manager-shadow:followup.

Interview Rubric Addendum (for hiring managers/promotions assessment):
- Use structured behavioral anchors for manager interviews (sample probes):
  - Tell me about a time you had to redirect a team mid-sprint. What was your process and outcome? (Probe for: stakeholder alignment, prioritization criteria, communication cadence.)
  - Describe a disagreement you had with your manager about team priorities. How did you handle it? (Probe for: upward influence, escalation judgment.)
  - Give an example of a time you provided hard feedback that improved performance. What did you say and how did you follow up? (Probe for: specificity, coaching loop.)
- Scoring guidance: 1–5 across: judgment, coaching, operational follow-through, cross-functional influence. Note concrete evidence (examples, names, dates) for scores >4.

Handoff templates (copy/paste-ready snippets):
- 1:1 agenda template: "ID / wins / blockers / career note / action items".
- Runbook update PR summary: "What changed, why, verification steps, rollback plan".
- Slack #team note to announce new manager: short bio + 3 priorities + ask for 1 intro.

Practical access checklist (people-ops quick actions):
- Okta: add to Managers group
- GitHub: add to team-admin (read/write to non-prod)
- Console: Console-read for team routes, cost dashboards; Console-admin only after 30-day sign-off
- PagerDuty/Oncall: shadow role in read-only for first 14 days
- HRIS: ensure manager has approvals flow enabled

Notes to self / open questions (work items):
- Q: Should manager get Console-admin on day 15 by default? Proposal: wait until 30-day review unless strongly needed.
- Q: What SLAs should access provisioning meet? Target: 48h from offer accept for all basics. If not met, escalate to people-ops manager.
- Action: create a tiny GH action to auto-create the evidence doc when mentor assigned (PR linked above).

Next steps & owners:
- People Ops (Priya) to pilot with two managers in Feb cohort and collect evidence doc artifacts.
- Engineering mentors (Ethan) to prototype the 7-day pairing checklist and report friction points.
- Product mentors (Maya) to add 2 scenario roleplays for cross-functional influence.

References & templates:
- onboarding templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-templates
- manager 1:1 cheat sheet (internal): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ONBOARD/manager-1-1-cheatsheet

Document history:
- v0.1 2025-01-08: initial draft (Priya)
- v0.2 2025-01-18: added rubric and day-by-day deliverables (Ethan)
- v0.3 2025-02-02: refined access checklist and pilot plan (Maya)

End of doc.
